title: KABWATA CDF ROAD WORKS GAIN MOMENTUM AS COMMUNITIES RALLY BEHIND PROJECTS
article_text: Momentum is building around the 2025 CDF road projects in Kabwata, where paving works have become a visible sign of progress for residents who have long awaited improved infrastructure. The upgraded internal roads are beginning to reshape movement within the constituency, creating an atmosphere of optimism among commuters and local businesses. Residents highlight how the improved roads are transforming daily routines, making trips to schools, clinics, and workplaces faster and far more reliable. Meanwhile, both the Local authority and the Kabwata Constituency Development Fund Committee officials remain optimistic that the ongoing improvements will anchor Kabwata’s long-term development agenda

title: LUSAKA PROVINCE MINISTER HANDS OVER NEWLY CONSTRUCTED KATAMBALALA MARKET IN MATERO, URGES FACILITY CARE AND MAINTENANCE
wards: Lima Ward 30; Ward 30; in Lima Ward 30
article_text: A newly constructed Katambalala Railside Market shelter, built with support from the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) in Lima Ward 30 of Matero Constituency, has officially been handed over to the community. The facility built at a total cost of K1.6 million, is expected to provide trading spaces for more than 300 traders who previously conducted business under harsh conditions in the open, exposed to rains and scorching sun. Presiding over the handover ceremony today, Lusaka Province Minister Hon. Sheal Mulyata said the new market shelter will enhance comfort and dignity for traders, boost economic activities in the area, attract more customers, increase business confidence and contribute to household incomes, thereby supporting the global goal of poverty reduction and inclusive growth. Hon. Mulyata noted that government has continued to demonstrate its unwavering commitment to improving citizens’ welfare through effective utilisation of the CDF, highlighting the increase in CDF allocation to K40 million per constituency in the 2026 national budget. The Minister emphasised that communities now have the power to propose, identify, plan and implement projects that directly respond to their needs, adding that the market is a practical example of decentralisation working effectively when local priorities are respected and supported. She observed that for many years, traders in Lima Ward operated under difficult conditions, exposed to extreme weather and unsanitary environments, which not only made trading challenging but also compromised the quality of goods and the health and safety of both traders and customers, saying the facility has now transformed this situation. Hon. Mulyata further urged the market committee and local leadership to work closely with the Lusaka City Council to enforce good management practices, maintain sanitation and ensure equitable access to trading spaces, further advising traders to clean the market and its surroundings daily to prevent disease outbreaks. Lusaka District Commissioner expressed delight at the development, saying she was proud that CDF had delivered much-needed infrastructure in Lusaka, more than in any other province, pledging continued support towards development initiatives. Meanwhile, Lima Ward 30 Councillor Daniel Mwewa said his ward was privileged, for the first time since independence to have such a facility that will enable traders to conduct business in a conducive environment. Councillor Mwewa commended government for the initiative, noting that his ward has greatly benefited from CDF projects, including the procurement of 400 desks, construction of a 1×4 classroom block at George Primary School and establishment of a skills centre in Chitukuko area. By Nyambe Bulumba Assistant Public Relations Manager 19/11/25

title: GOVERNMENT HANDS OVER MARKET SHELTER AT GARDEN CHILULU MARKET
wards: Chilulu Market in Ngwerere Ward 22; Ward 22
article_text: Lusaka District Commissioner, Dr. Rosa Kayuni Zulu, today officially handed over a newly constructed market shelter at Garden Chilulu Market in Ngwerere Ward 22, Mandevu Constituency. Represented by District Administrative Officer, Mr. On’eal Chiiya, Dr. Zulu described the project as a milestone in bringing development closer to the people, aligning with the Government’s Decentralization Policy and implemented through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Dr. Zulu highlighted that traders at Chilulu Market previously operated under harsh conditions, exposed to the elements and unsanitary environments. Ahe said the modern market shelter will transform the way business is conducted, providing a clean, safe and organized trading environment. At the same event, Mandevu Member of Parliament, Hon. Christopher Shakafuswa, expressed gratitude to President Hakainde Hichilema for his visionary leadership and commitment to community empowerment through the increased allocation of CDF. Hon. Shakafuswa is of the view that the enhanced CDF allocation has enabled constituencies to undertake projects that benefit the people and improve their livelihoods. The modern market shelter, constructed at a total cost of K818,546.12 is expected to accommodate over 48 traders. By Rose C. Samiselo

The LCC has made significant progress in the procurement process for furnishing the two centres, and they are expected to commence operations soon. title: SECOND CDF-FUNDED CLASSROOM BLOCK AT KABANANA PRIMARY SCHOOL ALMOST COMPLETE
article_text: The construction of a 1×4 classroom block at Kabanana Primary School in Mandevu Constituency, funded through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), has reached an advanced stage, with works currently standing at 85 percent completion. The project, valued at over K1.5 million, is structured in two phases. Phase One has been successfully completed, covering key structural components including flooring, plastering, roofing, window frame installation, and partial ceiling works. Phase Two is scheduled to commence next week and will focus on final finishes and fittings to bring the block to full operational readiness. Once completed, the new classroom block will significantly reduce congestion at the school, thereby enhancing the teaching and learning environment for both pupils and staff. This development marks the second classroom block constructed at Kabanana Primary School through the CDF, reinforcing the Council’s dedication to improving educational infrastructure across Lusaka District. The Council is impressed that the contractor, AGADA ZM Constructions Limited, is dedicated to completing the project on time and has adhered to the project’s terms of reference to ensure that the structure meets the expected standards and is durable and fit for purpose. The Council also calls upon the school management and the surrounding community to take collective responsibility in safeguarding this infrastructure against vandalism and misuse. Public assets must be protected to ensure their long-term benefit. The Lusaka City Council remains committed to fostering inclusive development and strengthening the education system through strategic investments in infrastructure to ensure building a resilient and empowered community. Issued by Chola Mwamba Public Relations Manager Lusaka City Council (LCC) 06/10/2025

title: CDF-FUNDED MADIMBA WATER RETICULATION PROJECT OFFICIALLY HANDED OVER
article_text: The Madimba Water Reticulation Project in Mwembeshi Ward 31 of Matero Constituency has officially been handed over to the community, following its successful completion under the 2023 Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Lusaka District Commissioner, Dr. Rosa Zulu, who was represented by District Administrative Officer Mr. O’Neal, presided over the handover ceremony held earlier today. Dr. Zulu commended the community for selecting a project that directly addresses a critical need, noting that the initiative will significantly improve water access in the area. She disclosed that the project, valued at K383,529.50, comprises two solar-powered boreholes installed at Dina Kayimba and Chunga Secondary School. “By investing in water infrastructure, the government is not only meeting a basic human need but also enhancing the overall well-being and productivity of the community,” Dr. Zulu stated. Matero Member of Parliament, Hon. Miles Sampa expressed satisfaction with the development, describing it as a timely intervention to address persistent water challenges in the Ward. Hon. Sampa noted that the use of solar-powered boreholes would ensure uninterrupted water supply, even during power outages. He further urged residents to safeguard the infrastructure to ensure its sustainability and long-term benefit to the community.

title: BAULENI MINI HOSPITAL POISED FOR MAJOR CONSTRUCTION WITH NEW MATERNITY WING AND MORTUARY
article_text: Bauleni township is on the verge of a healthcare breakthrough as two key Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects near completion at the Bauleni Mini Hospital in Lusaka Central Constituency. The projects fully funded under CDF, include the construction of a new Maternity Wing (Phase 1), being undertaken by Lewdan Investments Limited at a cost of K720,000, and the construction of a Mortuary, carried out by Rockfield Contractors Limited at a cost of K945,510. Both projects are at 90 percent completion. Once completed, the maternity wing will significantly improve maternal and child healthcare in the area, while the mortuary will be a historic first for Bauleni township, which has never had such a facility. The mortuary is expected to bring dignity to families and communities during difficult times, reducing the burden of transporting deceased loved ones to faraway facilities. Bauleni Mini Hospital already serves a population of over 4,000 people with 150 staff across various departments, including radiology, physiotherapy, and inpatient care. The new additions will not only expand the scope of services but also strengthen the hospital’s capacity to meet the growing healthcare demands of the community. These CDF investments are a clear demonstration of government’s commitment to improving access to quality health services at the community level. Residents of Bauleni and surrounding areas are set to benefit immensely once the facilities are officially opened.

title: MASSIVE ROAD CONSTRUCTION PROJECTS UNDERWAY IN LUSAKA AND NEIGHBORING DISTRICTS
article_text: Lusaka and its neighboring districts are currently undergoing a significant infrastructure facelift through various developmental projects, particularly in urban road rehabilitation and construction. Through different funding mechanisms, including the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) and other financial support from the central government, massive road upgrades are being extensively undertaken in Lusaka and neighboring districts. One of the roads being rehabilitated is the Great North Road. These projects aim to improve the city’s infrastructure, enhance road safety, and boost economic development. A safe and reliable road network is crucial for the transportation of people and goods, and the Council believes that these road works will have a positive impact on the city’s business environment. Some of the major roads currently under construction include the 40.1 km rehabilitation of urban roads, such as: Great East Road Acacia Road Ibex Road Main Street Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe Road Kamanga-Kapiliomba Road Once completed, these roads will improve the lives of citizens and create a conducive environment for businesses. The Council urges the public to bear with us during this period of construction and cooperate as we work towards delivering a better Lusaka for all. By Chola Mwamba

title: LUSAKA PROVINCIAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT OFFICER LAUDS CDF PROJECTS IN MATERO CONSTITUENCY
article_text: Lusaka Provincial Local Government Officer Charlston Hamulyata has expressed satisfaction with the effective implementation of Constituency Development Fund (CDF) projects in Matero Constituency. Leading a team of Lusaka City Council (LCC) CDF monitoring officers, Mr. Hamulyata said the carefully implemented projects will greatly benefit the community as they directly align with their needs. With CDF now decentralised, Mr. Hamulyata noted that the fund has become a game-changer for local development as communities are fully involved in identifying projects to be implemented. He said the initiative has been instrumental in driving development in Matero Constituency, with notable projects including infrastructure development, water and sanitation improvements, road rehabilitation and skills center facilities. Some of the specific projects visited by the team included the Kapwepwe Maternity block, classroom blocks at Desai Primary School and Chitanda School, a vegetable shelter at Mwamba Luchembe market and an ablution block at Edwin Mulongoti School. Mr. Hamulyata also encouraged students to take advantage of the skills development component of the CDF, urging them to apply for courses that will empower them to start their own businesses rather than waiting for employment. “This initiative aligns with the government’s vision to equip citizens with skills that will enable them to generate their own income,” he said. The Provincial Local Government Officer earlier this year, approved K17.6 million for 2025 CDF community projects in Matero Constituency, aimed at improving public infrastructure and services. The LCC team assured the community that all approved projects will be executed with high standards of quality and within agreed timeframes, underscoring the council’s dedication to bringing meaningful development to Matero Constituency. This demonstrates the government’s commitment to enhancing the lives of residents by providing access to better education, healthcare, security and public amenities.

title: Hon. Christopher Shakafuswa Monitors Progress of CDF Projects in Mandevu Constituency
article_text: Mandevu Constituency Member of Parliament Hon. Christopher Shakafuswa, today undertook a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation exercise of ongoing projects funded under the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). This initiative underscores his commitment to promoting good governance, transparency, and accountability in the utilization of public resources. The monitoring tour covered key infrastructure developments aimed at improving service delivery and the quality of life for residents of Mandevu. Projects inspected included: The construction of a maternity wing at Kabanana Health Post A mother’s shelter at Mandevu Clinic The ongoing Kasangula drainage works, and A 1×4 classroom block at Mutambe Primary School. Speaking during the tour, Hon. Shakafuswa emphasized the importance of ensuring that CDF-funded projects are implemented efficiently, meet the required standards, and serve the intended purpose for the community. The MP also encouraged community members to take an active role in monitoring local projects to strengthen civic participation and ownership.

title: MANDEVU COMMUNITY ENGAGED ON DEVELOPMENT INITIATIVE
article_text: Hon. Christopher Shakafuswa Member of Parliament for Mandevu Constituency, successfully conducted a four-day community engagement exercise across all eight (8) wards of the constituency. The engagement sessions which brought together the Member of Parliament, Ward Development Committee (WDC) members and Ward Councilors, served as a vital platform for direct interaction with residents. The objective of the meetings was to listen to the concerns of the community and gather input on priority development needs to be considered under the 2026 Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Throughout the engagements, residents in all eight wards expressed a range of development needs, highlighting key projects such as road rehabilitation, street lighting, Rehabilitation of car & foot bridges,Market Shelters, drainage improvements, upgrading of community schools, construction of police posts, and improved health facilities. Hon. Shakafuswa emphasized the importance of inclusive development engagements for they promote a broader effort to promote transparency, accountability, and community participation in the development process. The lawmaker also encouraged community members including persons with disabilities, to take advantage of the various skills training programs available under the CDF initiative, which are designed to empower individuals and promote self reliance. He reiterated his commitment to ensuring that the CDF responds to the actual needs of the people and supports projects that deliver real impact in the community. The MP expressed gratitude to all community members who took part in the meetings and reaffirmed his pledge to continue working hand in hand with the people of Mandevu to deliver meaningful and sustainable development. 📸 By Thandiwe Kalililo

title: GOVERNMENT PUSHES FOR INTEGRATED CDF IMS ROLLOUT: COLLABORATION KEY, SAYS LOCAL GOVERNMENT PERMANENT SECRETARY
article_text: The Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development Permanent Secretary for Technical Services, Mr. Nicholas Phiri, has urged local councils to promptly update their Constituency Development Fund (CDF) dashboards. Speaking when he officially opened the Orientation Workshop for the rollout of the Integrated Constituency Development Fund (CDF) Information Management System at the Civic Centre in Lusaka today, Mr. Phiri emphasised that CDF initiatives have significantly impacted many people’s lives. He stressed that such information should be readily available on council platforms like websites, enabling the public to appreciate the benefits. “Once you have updated your CDF dashboards, websites and other platforms, citizens will be well-informed and able to track CDF applications, making both your work and theirs easier in the process,” Mr. Phiri stated. He encouraged Local Authorities to adopt technology and innovation in capturing developmental data, noting that quality data is vital for informed decision-making and policy formulation. “The Ministry relies on you, as Local Authorities, for data that helps us formulate decisions responding to people’s needs and as such, ensure you provide us with up-to-date and quality data,” he explained. Mr. Phiri advised workshop participants to prioritise the program as it would aid their local authorities in addressing community challenges with relevant information. He also called for collaboration between Smart Zambia, the Ministry, local authorities and stakeholders to drive digital innovation for effective service delivery. The Permanent Secretary pledged the Ministry’s support for the initiative, including necessary resources like human capital and equipment.

title: LCC DELIVERS OVER 21,000 SCHOOL DESKS AND 130 CLASSROOMS ACROSS LUSAKA CONSTITUENCIES SINCE 2022
article_text: The Lusaka City Council (LCC) has made significant strides in improving the education sector through the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Between the years 2022 and 2025, the Council delivered 130 classrooms to 7 constituencies, enhancing the learning environment in various schools. This initiative has helped decongest overcrowded classrooms and accommodate new pupils, particularly with the implementation of the free education policy. The additional classrooms have provided a more conducive learning environment, enabling pupils to focus on their studies. In addition to the classrooms, the CDF has also provided 21,775 desks to schools across the 7 constituencies between 2022 and 2025. These desks have improved sitting arrangements for pupils, making them to learn in a more comfortable environment and eliminating the need for students to sit on the floor. The provision of desks and classrooms has had a positive impact on the education system in Lusaka. Students can now learn in a more comfortable and conducive environment, which is essential for their academic success. The Lusaka City Council’s commitment to delivering services to the public is evident in its efforts to improve the education sector. By providing classrooms and desks, the council is supporting the government’s initiative to provide free education and ensuring that students have access to quality learning facilities. Through the CDF, the Lusaka City Council continues to prioritize the needs of its citizens, particularly in the education sector. The council’s efforts to improve learning infrastructure will have a lasting impact on the lives of students and the community at large. Issued by: Chola Mwamba (Ms) Public Relations Manager Lusaka City Council (LCC) 19/09/25

title: MUNALI CONSTITUENCY EMBARKS ON DOCUMENTING CDF BURSARY SUCCESS STORIES
article_text: In a bid to showcase the impact of the Constituency Development Fund (CDF), Lusaka City Council’s District Planning Officer (DPO), Mr. Ronald Ngala has led a team of Council Officers on a tour to document bursary success stories from pupils and students sponsored through CDF under Munali Constituency. The exercise aims to highlight the transformative impact that CDF has had on learners and learning institutions. It also seeks to inform the general public on the importance of CDF, appreciate the learning environment, identify challenges and verify the presence of Munali beneficiaries in various institutions. So far, institutions visited include Northern Technical College (NORTEC), Technical and Vocational Teachers’ College, Kabwe Institute of Technology and Macha Secondary School. During the tour at Kabwe Institute of Technology, Mr. Ngala told Principal Officer Dr. Enerst Mubita that this visit was different from previous ones, noting that the focus was on documenting how CDF has positively transformed students’ lives and contributed to institutional development. “We are not only documenting bursary success stories but also assessing how the implementation of CDF has improved the learning experience and livelihood of our students,” said Mr. Ngala. Other institutions scheduled for visits include Choma Secondary School, Rusangu Secondary School, Luangwa, Secondary School among others. The documentation team comprises the Munali CDF Committee Chairperson, Mr. Auditor Mazuba, an Auditor, Socio-Economic Planners and the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer assigned to Munali Constituency.

title: MADIMBA WATER PROJECT TO IMPROVE SOURCE OF WATER FOR MWEMBESHI WARD
article_text: The Lusaka City Council (LCC) has made significant progress in addressing water challenges in Matero Constituency through the Madimba Water Reticulation Project. Funded by the 2023 Constituency Development Fund, the project involves drilling two solar-powered boreholes to supply clean water to the community. Previously, residents of Mwembeshi Ward in Matero Constituency relied on shallow wells, which posed health risks due to the potential for disease outbreaks like cholera and typhoid. The new boreholes, located at Dina Kaimba and Chunga Secondary School, will provide a reliable source of clean water for drinking and household use. The project, valued at approximately K300,000, is nearly complete, with a completion rate of 98%. It is expected to be finalized within the next month, bringing much-needed relief to the residents of Mwembeshi Ward. The Constituency Development Fund continues to play a vital role in driving local development across Zambia, supporting key sectors such as infrastructure, water, and sanitation. These initiatives demonstrate the government’s commitment to improving public services and infrastructure in Matero Constituency. By investing in water infrastructure, the government is not only meeting a fundamental need but also enhancing the overall health, well-being, and productivity of the community. The Madimba Water Reticulation Project showcases the transformative impact of CDF funding on local communities. The Lusaka City Council assures the community that all CDF-funded projects are being executed to high standards of quality and within agreed timeframes, reflecting the government’s dedication to improving the lives of its citizens.

title: OVER 300 CDF APPLICATION FORMS DISTRIBUTED AT THE AGRICULTURAL AND COMMERCIAL SHOW
article_text: OVER 300 CDF APPLICATION FORMS DISTRIBUTED AT THE AGRICULTURAL AND COMMERCIAL SHOW The Lusaka City Council has made significant strides in ensuring residents’ access to the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) with over 300 application forms distributed at the 97th Agricultural and Commercial Show. This initiative provides opportunities for residents to benefit from the fund across various categories, including Skills Development, Secondary School Bursaries, Loans and Grants. These categories support residents’ development, particularly for youths and women by providing them with resources to improve their livelihoods. The application window for the 2026 CDF is open and residents are encouraged to submit their applications before the August 30, 2025. deadline. The response to the applications has been overwhelming, with many residents showing interest in accessing the fund. To facilitate this, a CDF Desk has been strategically set up at the Show to provide information and assistance on the application process. The Council remains committed to ensuring a smooth application process and easy access to CDF information, promoting inclusive development and improving residents’ lives by providing opportunities to access the CDF.

title: the government is constructing the Kamwala Health Post using the Constituency Development Fund (CDF)
article_text: In an effort to provide accessible healthcare services to Kamwala South residents, the government is constructing the Kamwala Health Post using the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Significant progress has been made on the construction of the facility, which is steadily approaching completion. The health post is expected to enhance access to essential healthcare services for more than 50,000 residents of Kamwala South, Kamulanga and surrounding areas, offering a much-needed solution to longstanding challenges in accessing local medical care. Once operational, the facility is expected to reduce the burden on nearby health centers and minimise the long distances residents previously had to travel for basic medical care

title: EVALASTING YOUTH CLUB APPLAUDS GOVERNMENT FOR CDF EMPOWERMENT
wards: Phineas Walukowa of Kabanana Ward 27; Ward 27
article_text: A 2025 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) grant beneficiary under Mandevu Constituency, Mr. Phineas Walukowa of Kabanana Ward 27, has commended the Government for the continued support towards youth empowerment through the CDF initiative. Evalasting Youth Club, a cooperative group comprising 10 members (both men and women), was among the 113 cooperative groups in Mandevu that benefitted from the 2025 CDF allocation, which disbursed over K2.4 million in grants. The group received K22,000.00 which they invested in a poultry farming business. With the funds, they purchased 170 chicks and have since begun their operations. According to Mr. Walukowa, the project is progressing well, and the chickens will soon be ready for sale. Mr. Walukowa expressed profound gratitude to the Government, stating that the empowerment has significantly improved their livelihoods. He noted that the support has not only created employment within the community but has also enabled members to educate their children and enhance their economic stability. The Government continues to empower communities through the CDF, enabling them to prioritize and implement development projects that directly benefit their constituencies.

title: LUSAKA CITY COUNCIL ILLUMINATES ROADS WITH SOLAR STREET LIGHTS
article_text: The Lusaka City Council has taken a significant step towards enhancing road safety and security by installing 231 solar street lights in four constituencies, namely Kabwata, Lusaka Central, Mandevu, and Matero. The installations of the solar powered lights were done between 2022 and 2024 using the Constituency Development Fund (CDF) at a cost of K8,177,169.00. This initiative aims to improve visibility on roads, particularly at night, and reduce accidents caused by poor visibility. Additionally, by adopting solar-powered street lights, the council is promoting sustainability and reducing dependence on a traditional electric power supply. The installation of solar powered lights is part of the council’s broader efforts to enhance urban infrastructure and services, creating a safer environment for road users, pedestrians, and residents while contributing to the city’s development and beautification. The Lusaka City Council plans to extend this initiative to other constituencies, furthermore enhancing road safety, promoting sustainability, and improving residents’ quality of life. The local authority is committed to investing in effective and sustainable road infrastructure for the betterment of the city.

title: 𝑾𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒏’𝒔 𝑪𝒉𝒊𝒄𝒌𝒆𝒏 𝑹𝒆𝒂𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝑽𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆 𝑻𝒖𝒓𝒏𝒔 𝑷𝒐𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒕𝒚 𝒊𝒏𝒕𝒐 𝑷𝒓𝒐𝒔𝒑𝒆𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝑻𝒉𝒓𝒐𝒖𝒈𝒉 𝑪𝑫𝑭 𝑺𝒖𝒑𝒑𝒐𝒓𝒕
wards: Ward 20; the club based in Roma Ward 20
article_text: In a powerful testament to resilience and determination, a group of ten women has defied the odds, rising from financial hardships through poultry farming after securing a K24,000 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) grant in 2022. Margret Simuyandi, Chairperson of the club, recounts how the journey began, with unwavering hope and a well-prepared business proposal presented to the Ward Development Committee (WDC). Against stiff competition, the club based in Roma Ward 20 of Mandevu Constituency, emerged victorious, earning the grant that would breathe life into their ambitions. With excitement and newfound resources, the group initially rented a chicken run and launched their venture with 200 birds, brimming with optimism. However, the road was anything but smooth. Disease swept through their flock, devastating their numbers and leaving them with a mere 60 survivors. Adding to their struggles, two employed youths, entrusted with managing the poultry, failed to meet expectations, causing further setbacks. Yet, in the face of adversity, giving up was never an option. Determined to rewrite their fate, the women embraced resilience. They pivoted their operations, constructing a new chicken run utilising the Chairlady’s bare land, turning personal space into a beacon of hope. With renewed vigor, they expanded their flock, gradually increasing their numbers to between 200 and 300 birds per cycle, ensuring steady sales and a sustainable livelihood. Today, their efforts are paying off, providing financial stability and better lives for their families. What began as a humble poultry project has evolved into a thriving business, demonstrating the power of persistence. Grateful for the empowerment, the group expresses deep appreciation to the government for the CDF grant, which they say has transformed their lives and steered them away from poverty. But they are not stopping here, their sights are set on broader horizons. With aspirations reaching beyond poultry, they now plan to venture into full-scale agriculture targeting maize farming, determined to further expand their dreams and economic opportunities

title: The government has commenced the construction of a mortuary at Bauleni Mini Hospital.
article_text: In an effort to address the challenges of mortuary services in Bauleni and surrounding areas in Lusaka Central Constituency, the government has commenced the construction of a mortuary at Bauleni Mini Hospital. The project, currently at foundation level, is being funded using the 2025 Constituency Development Fund (CDF). The facility will help reduce the long distances residents previously had to travel to access these services.

title: LCC SOON TO COMMISSION 14 NEW HEALTH FACILITIES ACROSS LUSAKA
article_text: LCC SOON TO COMMISSION 14 NEW HEALTH FACILITIES ACROSS LUSAKA The Lusaka City Council (LCC) is on the verge of completing and commissioning 14 health facilities constructed across the seven constituencies in Lusaka, designed to improve healthcare delivery. The health facilities, which include maternity wings and admission wards, have been constructed at a total cost of K12,576,210.4 using the Constituency Development Fund (CDF). Among these facilities, which are almost at completion level, are the Kabwata Maternity Wing, Health Post in John Laing, Maternity Wing in John Howard, Admission Ward at Freedom Clinic, Mutendere, and Grips Clinic Phase 2, among others. The 14 health facilities will help improve access to health services and reduce the costs residents spend on traveling long distances to access medical care. Furthermore, the maternity wings will enhance maternal care for expectant mothers in the city. In line with the Ministry of Local Government and Rural Development, the Lusaka City Council is committed to ensuring the timely commissioning of all CDF projects in the city. This initiative underscores the council’s dedication to enhancing the quality of life for residents and providing essential services that cater to their needs.

title: LCC Completes Chifundo Road drainage system, near completion of Lilayi close road project
wards: Ward 4; drainage system in Lilayi Ward 4
article_text: LCC COMPLETES CHIFUNDO ROAD DRAINAGE SYSTEM, NEARS COMPLETION OF LILAYI CLOSE ROAD PROJECT The Lusaka City Council (LCC) has completed the construction of the Chifundo Road drainage system in Chawama Constituency, funded by the 2023 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) at a total cost of K2.3 million. Additionally, the construction of the 2.2-kilometer Lilayi Close Road and accompanying drainage system in Lilayi Ward 4, Chawama Constituency, is nearing completion. The project involves grading and upgrading the road to standard gravel and is funded under the 2024 Constituency Development Fund (CDF) at a total cost of K2.5 million. The project is currently 85% complete and is expected to be ready for commissioning soon. These projects will significantly benefit the community by reducing flooding, enhancing transportation and supporting local businesses. These initiatives have also led to the creation of more than 100 jobs during the construction phase and paved the way for sustainable development in the constituency. We therefore urge the residents to take an active role in preserving these infrastructures and to avoid dumping garbage into the drainage systems to maintain their functionality. The City Council reaffirms its dedication to improving the lives of Lusaka residents through the efficient utilization of CDF. The Local Authority remains committed to implementing similar projects in all constituencies, subject to identification by residents and approval by authorities to ensure the continued growth and development of Lusaka’s infrastructure.
